editorial.thesis: A hospitality-and-motor-trade city of about 896,000. Its retail is heavy on banks & atms and cafés, tea & coffee, and thin on pharmacy & health retail and grocery & daily needs — and 54% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 38% of Bengaluru's. 23.76 chain outlets per lakh residents against 63.31 in Bengaluru; 31 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by MedPlus 31, Apollo Pharmacy 25, Domino's 18.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 7.9% (Bengaluru 4.0%); automotive 4.0% (Bengaluru 2.8%); offices 7.5% (Bengaluru 12.7%); malls & department stores 0.3% (Bengaluru 0.5%). Raw counts would mislead because Bengaluru is mapped more completely (108,499 places against 9,717), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 8 zones hold 54% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Hebbal Layout alone has about 86,000 residents and 42 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Bengaluru. 48% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Bengaluru 40%). The largest cores are Krishna Rajendra Circle (828 places) and Kuvempunagar Ii Stage (590).

The widest brand gaps against Bengaluru. Apollo Pharmacy 25 outlets vs 283; MedPlus 31 outlets vs 273; Café Coffee Day 15 outlets vs 221. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Bengaluru, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Hebbal Layout and Udayagiri are the largest zones by residents (86,000 and 68,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 48% of all commercial places, and Krishna Rajendra Circle alone lists 828.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Ptc Campus · Ittigegud holds 26 of the 213 tracked chain outlets, and Krishna Rajendra Circle adds 23.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Kuvempunagar Ii Stage and Udayagiri lead on education places (83 and 60, with 35 and 14 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Hebbal Layout and Udayagiri. The blue cores include Krishna Rajendra Circle.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (108,499 places in Bengaluru against 9,717 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Bengaluru; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Bengaluru, Mysuru's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (7.9% vs 4.0%), automotive (4.0% vs 2.8%), banks & finance (8.2% vs 6.6%) and under-index on offices (7.5% vs 12.7%), malls & department stores (0.3% vs 0.5%), grocery & daily needs (1.9% vs 2.5%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 213 outlets of 31 tracked national brands within 8 km — 23.76 per lakh residents against Bengaluru's 63.31 (2535 outlets of 51 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Bengaluru are Apollo Pharmacy (25 vs 283); MedPlus (31 vs 273); Café Coffee Day (15 vs 221). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Bengaluru's, so low means thin by Bengaluru's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Mysuru's age mix against Bengaluru: children (0–14) 20.9% vs 22.8%, 15–24 19.5% vs 19.5%, working age 49.5% vs 50.2%, 60+ 10.1% vs 7.5%. Under-25s are 40% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 6.4% of mapped places against 7.0% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 18 (Bengaluru 193), KFC 10 (Bengaluru 83), Pizza Hut 6 (Bengaluru 99), McDonald's 5 (Bengaluru 76).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.9% of mapped places against 2.6% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 15 (Bengaluru 221), Starbucks 2 (Bengaluru 42).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.7% of mapped places against 0.8% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 3 (Bengaluru 67).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.9% of mapped places against 2.5% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 12 (Bengaluru 64), DMart 5 (Bengaluru 37), Easyday 4 (Bengaluru 3), Big Bazaar 3 (Bengaluru 18).
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.9% of mapped places against 1.4% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: MedPlus 31 (Bengaluru 273), Apollo Pharmacy 25 (Bengaluru 283).
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.7% of mapped places against 5.1% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Trends 16 (Bengaluru 146), Bata 14 (Bengaluru 130), Raymond 7 (Bengaluru 78), Westside 4 (Bengaluru 20).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.2% of mapped places against 6.6% in Bengaluru — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.5% of mapped places against 2.4% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.4% of mapped places against 3.8% in Bengaluru — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
